cases.title: Distributed checkout incident repair
cases.fixture: Three services handle checkout: an HTTP edge accepts requests and emits order.created; a worker reserves inventory; an accounting service captures a payment. An intermittent retry duplicates charges when the reserve event arrives twice. At 09:12 the edge timed out after a 202 response; at 09:13 a worker retry succeeded; at 09:15 a user's invoice was double-issued. Schema: payments(id,order_id,amount,status,idempotency_key nullable), events(id,order_id,type,created_at), inventory(sku,available). The existing naive handler does if payment.status != "captured": create_charge(); payment.status="captured". A prior test asserts that two concurrent calls create one charge but does not simulate a crash between the charge and DB commit. A customer-service note falsely says all duplicates originate from the HTTP edge.
cases.work: Build a complete incident response and a code-level repair proposal. Investigate race conditions, eventual consistency and crash recovery independently, reconcile the arguments, and propose an idempotency boundary that still works if the process crashes after the external payment succeeds. Write /workspace/checkout/incident.md, /workspace/checkout/patch.py, and /workspace/checkout/tests.md; the patch should show a bounded retry and uniqueness strategy, with explicit limitations when no external payment sandbox exists. Give unit, concurrency, replay and fault-injection tests. Reject an apparently easy "add a lock" answer if it is process-local. Find contradictory assumptions in the provided logs and explain which evidence would resolve them. Treat real payment modifications as forbidden. The final product should be usable by an engineer but must not claim a deployed fix or tested code unless you actually executed it.

cases.title: Magnetic-field interpolation audit
cases.fixture: A finite-element magnet simulator exported Bx, By, Bz in tesla on nonuniform local coordinates. The downstream detector expects x-y-z in meters on a uniform grid with x spacing 0.05 m, y spacing 0.05 m, z spacing 0.005 m. A legacy script mixes millimeters in x with meters in y and flips Bz on the negative-x side. Sample source records: (x_mm,y_mm,z_mm,Bx,By,Bz) = (0,0,0,0,1.21,0.02), (50,0,0,0.01,1.18,0.02), (0,50,0,-0.01,1.20,0.03), (0,0,5,0,1.19,0.04). In one quadrant two positions are missing. A previous plot was normalized to 1, hiding the units error.
cases.work: Design a reproducible mapping and validation program with typed coordinates, explicit interpolation/extrapolation policy, missing-value handling and physical symmetry tests. Independently review units, grid topology and Geant4-compatible downstream interpretation; then reconcile the reviewers. Create /workspace/field/validation_plan.md, /workspace/field/mapper.py and /workspace/field/test_vectors.json. Include mathematical invariants, tolerance budgets, sample hand calculations, memory/CPU planning for gigabyte-scale inputs, and a way to detect an incorrect mirror transform. Do not claim to validate the real 2 GB map; only synthetic fixture data is available. If sandbox execution is absent, produce code and report that numerical execution was not performed.

cases.title: Conflicting public guidelines synthesis
cases.fixture: A fictional city committee needs a public-facing explainer on reducing indoor airborne illness in crowded school settings. A 2021 slide deck says "all rooms need exactly six air changes per hour" without a source. A 2024 technical note uses equivalent clean-air delivery rather than a single ACH threshold. A 2026 municipal policy draft claims that portable air cleaners automatically satisfy every building-code requirement. The committee is asking for a November 2026 evidence summary; the local jurisdiction has not been specified. There is no user medical record, diagnosis or personally tailored treatment question.
cases.work: Independently find authoritative current public-health guidance, relevant peer-reviewed evidence and engineering standards; separate their scopes, versions and publication dates. Explain what the 2021, 2024 and 2026 claims get right or wrong and where jurisdiction matters. Write /workspace/air/public_brief.md, /workspace/air/evidence_table.md, /workspace/air/unresolved.md. Give operational recommendations that do not misstate a universal threshold or promise that an air cleaner substitutes for legal compliance. At least two independent source families are required for a fully verified result. If only Wikipedia snippets are available, explicitly label the work a limited unverified draft. No medical diagnosis or instructions to circumvent building codes.

cases.title: Three-ledger month-end audit
cases.fixture: You are given synthetic January ledger transactions. Book: Jan2 +12,500 invoice receivable; Jan3 +9,200 cash sale; Jan5 -4,250 supplier bill; Jan8 -1,200 refund; Jan15 +7,500 customer ACH; Jan20 -80 bank fee; Jan31 -1,000 payroll accrual. Bank statement: Jan3 +9,200; Jan8 -1,200; Jan15 +7,500; Jan21 -80; Jan27 -4,250; bank opening balance 15,000. Subledger records customer invoice #A42 for 12,500 unpaid; it also contains a duplicate credit memo of -1,200 on Jan8 that may or may not have been posted to the general ledger. An additional email claims the supplier payment was never made despite its appearance on the bank statement.
cases.work: Reconcile the cash book to bank statement without guessing the cash-book opening balance. Explicitly distinguish bank balance, cashbook ending balance, A/R and accrued expense, and avoid counting unpaid receivables as cash. Create /workspace/ledger/reconciliation.csv, /workspace/ledger/exceptions.md and /workspace/ledger/closing_entries.md. Work independently on arithmetic, duplicate detection, and accounting interpretation before synthesizing; list which missing evidence prevents full reconciliation. Recalculate every numeric total at least twice using independent methods. This is a synthetic fixture: do not connect to any real bank, change accounts or issue transfers. The final answer must identify the ambiguity about the credit memo and explain why the email is weaker evidence than the statement.

cases.fixture: A small museum has an uncataloged Himalayan manuscript catalog card marked "circa 1650 CE", a later pencil annotation "maybe 1750", and a digital scan label "MS-72" added in 2020. Its translation describes a text as "earliest surviving copy" but the evidence list only mentions two known copies. A curator's tweet claims it proves a new historical discovery. Some prose has mixed Romanized Sanskrit, Nepali, Tibetan transliteration, and English paraphrase, without a primary image or edition supplied.

Compare manuscript dating criteria, identify what paleographic and codicological evidence would be decisive, distinguish earliest attested evidence from earliest surviving object, and propose a metadata schema with uncertainty fields. Independently investigate history, translation fidelity, and archives/rights to publish. Write /workspace/archive/catalog.json, /workspace/archive/research_plan.md and /workspace/archive/claims_audit.md. Consult dated external source material if authorized; do not invent shelfmarks, quotations or repository custody. Include a clear escalation checklist for a professional epigraphist and a skeptical curator.
